Judgment

1. Vide this judgment, I propose to dispose of the instant appeal filed u/s 71 of The Food Safety &
Standard Act, 2006 against the impugned order dated 16.03.2018 passed by Adjudicating Officer/Additional District Magistrate (North), DM (North) Office Complex, Alipur, Delhi, whereby the appellant has been imposed penalty of Rs.75,000/ under Section 54 of the Food Safety Act,
2006.
2.

entities.text: Additional District Magistrate (North), DM (North) Office Complex, Alipur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The facts in brief are that on 22.08.2017, the FSO purchased a sample of "Boiled Mattar", an article of food for analysis from Sh. Surender Pal S/o Sh. Deep Chand, Food Business Operator cumIncharge from the premises of M/s Parag Self Help Group, House No. 758, Gali No. 7, Rajiv Colony, Narela, Delhi110 082.
Allegedly, Sh. Surender Pal was found manufacturing and storing the article of food for sale for human consumption at the time of taking the sample.

The sample of the article of food was divided into four equal parts and then put in four clean and dry glass bottles after mixing the "Boiled Mattar"
properly with the help of a clean and dry steel Karchhi and was added forty drops of formalin in each sample bottle and each bottle of sample was packed, fastened and sealed according to the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and rules made thereunder.

The FBO's signatures were obtained on the D.O. Slip and wrapper of the Surender Pal vs Food Safety Officer on 14 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107299970/
1 bottle containing the sample.

entities.text: Surender Pal vs Food Safety Officer
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Notice in Form VA was given to Sh. Surender Pal and the price of the sample was also offered to him vide Credit Note dated 22.08.2017 but he did not accept it stating that it was to be used for Aanganwadi children.
3. Allegedly, the FBO disclosed that sample food article was prepared under him as Incharge.
Panchnama was prepared and all documents were prepared by the FSO and signed by the FBO.
Since no independent person was ready to join the proceedings, Sh. Anil Kumar, Process Server joined the proceedings as a witness.

4. On 23.08.2017, one counterpart of the sample in intact condition along with copy of memo in Form VI in sealed packed and another copy of memo in Form VI under separate sealed cover were sent separately to the Food Analyst, Delhi.
The other two counterparts of the sample along with two copies of memos in Form VI were deposited with the designated officer Sh. Satish Kumar Gupta in intact condition.

The FBO did not request to send the fourth counterpart of the sample for analysis from an NABL Accredited Laboratory under Rule 2.4.5 of the Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011 and, therefore, the fourth counterpart was also deposited with the designated officer.

5. The Food Analyst vide report dated 29.08.2017 opined that the sample contained extraneous matter, namely, one hair in contravention of Section 26(2)(ii) read with definition of extraneous matter as defined under Section 3(1)(i) of the Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006.

The opportunity was given to the FBO for filing an appeal against the report of the Food Analyst under Section 46(4)
of the FSS Act, 2006 for sending one part of the sample to the Referral Food Laboratory.

However,
the FBO did not prefer any appeal against the report.
6. The complainant alleged that Sh. Surender Pal was Incharge and responsible for conduct of business and was looking after daytoday business at the time of taking the sample.

The FSO thus,
filed the complaint against the appellant for having committed the offence violating the provisions of Sections 26(1), 26(2)(ii) and 27(1) of the Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006 read with Section 3(1)(i) of the said Act, punishable under Section 54 of the said Act.

7. The FSO and appellant appeared before the Adjudicating Officer and the Adjudicating Officer after perusing the Food Analysis Report held that the appellant has committed offence/violated the provisions of Sections 26(1), 26(2)(ii) and 27(1) of the Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006 read with Section 3(1)(i) of the said Act, punishable under Section 54 of the said Act.

8. The Adjudicating Officer after taking into account Section 54 of the Food Safety Act, 2006,
imposed a penalty of Rs.75,000/ upon the appellant.

9. The appellant challenged this impugned order on the ground that in fact this activity was being carried out in pursuance to the tripartite agreement between the Department of Women & Child Development, GNCT of Delhi as first party, The People Welfare Society; a Mother NonProfit Organization as second party and 03 SHGs as third party.

As per this agreement, the Department of Women and Child Development engaged the non profit organization, namely, The People Welfare Society to prepare and distribute the supplementary nutrition in the Aanganwari Centres of ICDS Surender Pal vs Food Safety Officer on 14 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107299970/
2 project at Narela, Delhi by setting up/building capacity of Self Help Group of women only.
10.

sentences.text: In pursuance to this scheme of Self Help Group, the name 'Parag' was created to give job to the underprivileged women of the society, which was consisting ten women who take care of the preparation of food and were fully responsible for the activities relating to food preparation for Aanganwari Centres.

11. The appellant has stated that the FSO has not impleaded any member of the Self Help Group i.e.
'Parag'.
It has further been submitted that he was only a link between the Self Help Group and Mother NonProfit Organization and all the acts pertaining to food preparation were done by such Self Help Group.
The materials on daily basis were also purchased in the name of such Self Help Group.
The appellant has submitted that he put his signatures on the documents as per instruction of the respondent, as he is only 8th standard pass.
It has further been submitted by the appellant that there is nothing on record to suggest that he, in any manner, contacted with any activity of the preparation of food.
It has also been submitted that the Adjudicating Officer has unjustifiably imposed heavy fine upon him.

12. Per contra, Ld. Chief PP for the State/respondent has submitted that the appellant has represented himself as FBO and at no point of time he took plea before the Adjudicating Officer that he was not the Incharge and responsible for the conduct of business.
13. I have considered the submission and perused the record carefully.
14. I consider that the plea taken by the appellant at this stage is liable to be rejected outrightly.

Perusal of the appeal itself indicates that the appellant himself has stated in the appeal that he was working with nonprofit organization, namely, The People Welfare Society without any salary in the capacity of Supervisor.
It has further been submitted for the appellant that he was only given the actual expenses incurred by him.
This admission of the appellant is sufficient to hold that he was responsible for dayto day affairs of the activities being carried out.
It would not make any difference if the appellant was paid only the actual expenses incurred by him or he occasionally visited the centre to sort out the difficulties of Self Help Group.
15. Accordingly, I do not find any illegality or infirmity in the impugned order.
Counsel for the appellant has also argued on the point of sentence.
It has been argued that in fact the appellant was not getting remuneration and the fine imposed by the Adjudicating Officer is on higher side.

Section 49 of the Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006 reads as under:
49. General provisions relating to penalty.
While adjudging the quantum of penalty under this Chapter, the Adjudicating Officer or the Tribunal, as the case may be, shall have due regard to the following:

3

sentences.text:
(a) The amount of gain or unfair advantage, wherever quantifiable, made as a result of the contravention,
(b) The Amount of loss caused or likely to cause to any person as a result of the contravention,
(c) The repetitive nature of the contravention,
(d) Whether the contravention is without his knowledge, and (e) Any other relevant factor.
17.
The Legislature in its wisdom provides many parameters to decide the quantum of fine imposed.
In the present case, it is a matter of record that the activities were being carried out in pursuance to the tripartite agreement between the Government, NonProfit Organization and Self Help Group.
The food was being prepared for the Aanganwari.
There seems to be no profit motive in the entire chain of activities.
The appellant has also stated that he was not getting any salary and was being paid only the actual expenses incurred by him.
I consider that the penalty imposed upon the appellant may be reduced to Rs.5000/.
Accordingly, the penalty imposed upon the appellant is modified to the extent that he shall pay Rs.5000/ as penalty.
18. The appeal is partly allowed.
Record of Adjudicating Officer/Additional District Magistrate (North) along with copy of the judgment be sent back.
19. File of appeal be consigned to Record Room.
Announced in open Court (DINESH KUMAR SHARMA) on 14.02.2020.
